quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONNECTED SPEECH PHENOMENON IN THE PHRASE
quests.hint: Notice what happens to /t/ in 'that' right before 'meal'. Exactly which place does it move to?
quests.explanation: When /t/ is followed by a bilabial consonant, speakers often shift its place of articulation to match. That's why the /t/ at the end of "that" becomes /p/ before "meal".
quests.phoneticRule: In fast speech, native speakers blend and drop sounds to speak more smoothly.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONNECTED SPEECH PHENOMENON IN THE PHRASE
quests.hint: 'you' has no 'w' in its spelling at all. So if you hear a /w/ before 'and I', where did it come from?

quests.phoneticRule: In fast speech, native speakers blend and drop sounds to speak more smoothly.
